adjudication_records.issue_text: dualwriter_mode3.go Create error path: on Storage.Create failure, recordLegacyDuration is called instead of recordStorageDuration, misattributing storage errors to the legacy metric

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Create() measures storage create latency with startStorage := time.Now() and calls d.Storage.Create(...). In the error branch (if err != nil), it logs the storage error but then calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). This uses the legacy metric recorder for a storage operation failure/latency, while the success path correctly calls d.recordStorageDuration(..., startStorage). This mismatch misattributes Storage.Create failures to legacy metrics and is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dualwriter_mode3.go Update error path: Storage.Update failure records via recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DualWriterMode3.Update measures the unified store call with `startStorage := time.Now()` and then calls `d.Storage.Update(...)`. On the error path (`if err != nil { ... }`), it records the duration using `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. This is inconsistent with the timing source (storage) and the success path immediately below which correctly uses `d.recordStorageDuration(...)`. Therefore the proposed finding (wrong metric function on Storage.Update failure) is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dualwriter_mode3.go async legacy write goroutines derive context from request ctx via WithTimeoutCause, so the legacy write is cancelled when the handler returns; should use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a detached context, otherwise legacy and unified storage silently diverge

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now return immediately after writing to Storage and then start a goroutine to write to Legacy. That goroutine’s context is derived from the incoming request ctx via context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...). If the caller cancels ctx when the handler returns (common for request-scoped contexts), the goroutine’s ctx will be canceled immediately despite the added timeout, causing the legacy write to be skipped/aborted and allowing divergence. This behavior is directly introduced by the diff (async legacy writes + inherited ctx).

adjudication_records.issue_text: dualwriter_mode3.go goroutines: errors from async legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection are only counted in a metric and never logged, unlike the previous implementation, making store divergence undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes are now performed asynchronously in goroutines for Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection. Inside those goroutines, the code only calls d.recordLegacyDuration(...) (and in DeleteCollection even calls d.recordStorageDuration(...) for the legacy call) and does not log the legacy error at all. Previously, synchronous legacy operations logged failures (e.g., Create: log.WithValues(...).Error(err, ...), Update: log.Error(errLeg,...), Delete: log.WithValues(...).Error(errLS,...), DeleteCollection: log.WithValues(...).Error(err,...)). This diff therefore removes error logging for legacy failures, making it harder to diagnose divergence unless you’re watching metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dualwriter_mode3.go Update goroutine: objInfo and caller-supplied obj/validation closures are used from a detached goroutine after the handler returns; apiserver may reuse/mutate these and objInfo.UpdatedObject is not guaranteed goroutine-safe or idempotent; the old updateWrapper pre-computation safeguard was removed

dualwriter_mode3.go Update: legacy Update receives the original objInfo rather than a wrapper carrying the object returned by Storage, so legacy store gets a different object (e.g. without resourceVersion/UID) and the two stores can drift

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In dualwriter_mode3.go, Update was changed from explicitly passing a wrapper containing the object returned by Storage.Update to Legacy.Update, to instead calling Legacy.Update with the original objInfo (see removed updateWrapper logic and new goroutine calling d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...)). This means legacy may compute/apply an update based on different input than the final persisted Storage result (e.g., missing server-assigned fields like resourceVersion/UID or based on a different “old” object), which can cause the legacy store to drift or even fail optimistic concurrency checks. The diff shows the previous code was deliberately ensuring legacy received the Storage-updated object, and that safeguard is now gone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dualwriter_mode3.go: fire-and-forget goroutines are untracked; Destroy() cannot wait for them so in-flight legacy writes may be dropped on shutdown, and there is no bound on concurrent legacy writes under load

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the new Mode3 implementation starts background goroutines for legacy writes in Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection (each uses `go func() { ... d.Legacy.<op>(...) ... }()`). These goroutines are not tracked (no WaitGroup/channel/worker pool) and there is no concurrency limiter; under load, every request can spawn an additional goroutine performing a legacy write. Because they are fire-and-forget and not tracked, there is no mechanism in this code for a shutdown path (e.g., Destroy) to wait for completion, so in-flight legacy writes can be abandoned if the process exits while goroutines are still running.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dualwriter_mode1_test.go:138 and mode3 tests: removed `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` leaves `p` undefined in TestMode1_Get and TestMode3_Create/List/Delete/DeleteCollection/Update; if a shared package-level registry is used instead, repeated NewDualWriter calls will panic with AlreadyRegisteredError

dualwriter_mode3_test.go: no test asserts the legacy store is actually written for Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection; tests would pass even if async legacy writes never happen, and legacy mocks are set up but AssertExpectations is never called

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: in the new pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go, several tests set up legacy expectations via testify/mock (e.g., TestMode3_Create.setupLegacyFn and TestMode3_Update.setupLegacyFn) but never call m.AssertExpectations(t) / mock.AssertExpectationsForObjects, nor do they otherwise assert legacy methods were invoked. Given the mode3 implementation now performs legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines (Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection), these tests will still pass even if the legacy calls never occur (or don’t occur before the test ends), because testify/mock does not fail on unmet expectations unless assertions are executed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dualwriter_mode3_test.go: Delete/DeleteCollection tests set no legacy expectation, so the background goroutine calling an unexpected mock method may panic after the subtest completes

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Delete and DeleteCollection, the implementation now spawns a background goroutine that calls the Legacy storage (d.Legacy.Delete / d.Legacy.DeleteCollection) on successful unified-store operations. In dualwriter_mode3_test.go, the success-path tests for Delete and DeleteCollection only set mock expectations for the Storage methods and set no expectations for the corresponding Legacy methods. The tests use a single testify mock.Mock (m := &mock.Mock{}) for both legacyStoreMock and storageMock; with no expected call registered, testify/mock will treat the Legacy call as unexpected and (since m.Test(t) is not set) typically panics. Because the call happens in a goroutine, this panic can occur after the subtest finishes, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dualwriter_mode3_test.go: TestMode3_List case name says 'not implemented' but tests a generic error; misleading label

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go, TestMode3_List has a test case name "error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented" while the test actually mocks Storage.List to return a generic error ("error") and asserts that error propagates. The implementation of List in dualwriter_mode3.go is present in the diff (it calls d.Storage.List), so the phrase "not implemented" is misleading, but this is only a test description string and does not affect behavior or correctness.
